```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(penalties7)
set.seed(1)
```

A penalty is $\rho(D\beta;\theta)$: a linear map, a scalar function of the
mapped coefficients, and hyperparameters of its own. In many R packages that
fit a penalized model, the penalty is written inside the fitting function as
a term of the objective, and its kinks, its rank and the dependence of its
value on the hyperparameters are not available outside that function. In
penalties7 the penalty is an object, and a fitting layer reads these
quantities from it to choose a fitting scheme.

This vignette builds a penalty that the package does not ship, writes the
methods that it has to supply, and shows what the base class and
`check_penalty()` provide in return. The example is the Berhu, the reverse
Huber penalty of Owen (2007):

$$\rho(\beta) = \begin{cases}
  \lambda\lvert\beta\rvert, & \lvert\beta\rvert \le \delta,\\[2pt]
  \lambda\dfrac{\beta^2 + \delta^2}{2\delta}, & \lvert\beta\rvert > \delta,
\end{cases}$$

which is the lasso near the origin and a ridge away from it. The kink at zero
sets small coefficients exactly to zero. In the tails the penalty grows
quadratically, so a large coefficient is shrunk in proportion to its size, as
under a ridge penalty, while the lasso shrinks every nonzero coefficient by
the same amount.

## The class and its constructor

```{r}
BerhuPenalty <- S7::new_class("BerhuPenalty", parent = penalty)

berhu_penalty <- function(n_coef, map = NULL) {
  BerhuPenalty(
    penalty_name = "berhu",
    map = map,
    n_coef = as.integer(n_coef),
    params = c("lambda", "delta"),
    params_bounds = list(lambda = c(0, Inf), delta = c(0, Inf)),
    link_params = list(lambda = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
                       delta = linkfunctions7::log_link()),
    params_smooth = c(lambda = TRUE, delta = TRUE)
  )
}
```

`params_bounds` holds open intervals, and `link_params` holds, for each
hyperparameter, the link that maps its interval onto the unconstrained scale
on which an outer search moves. `params_smooth` records the hyperparameters
in which the value is differentiable. It is stored with the object, and
`check_penalty()` does not read it: the validator places its grid from
`penalty_kinks()`.

## The methods

Each of the generics below that takes `theta` aligns it before it dispatches.
The generic reorders the list to `pen@params`, strips stray names off the
values, checks that each value is a single number inside `params_bounds`,
and, where it also takes `beta`, checks that `beta` has length `pen@n_coef`.
A method therefore receives a list in the penalty's own order and does not
align it again. One helper reads the list and records the branch in which
each coefficient falls, and the six methods for the value and the derivatives
share it:

```{r}
.berhu <- function(pen, beta, theta) {
  list(lam = theta$lambda, del = theta$delta,
       a = abs(beta), big = abs(beta) > theta$delta)
}
```

The next three methods supply the value, the gradient in $\beta$ and the
Hessian in $\beta$:

```{r}
S7::method(penalty_value, BerhuPenalty) <- function(pen, beta, theta, ...) {
  p <- .berhu(pen, beta, theta)
  sum(ifelse(p$big, p$lam * (beta^2 + p$del^2) / (2 * p$del), p$lam * p$a))
}

S7::method(penalty_gradient, BerhuPenalty) <- function(pen, beta, theta, ...) {
  p <- .berhu(pen, beta, theta)
  ifelse(p$big, p$lam * beta / p$del, p$lam * sign(beta))
}

S7::method(penalty_hessian, BerhuPenalty) <- function(pen, beta, theta, ...) {
  p <- .berhu(pen, beta, theta)
  diag(ifelse(p$big, p$lam / p$del, 0), length(beta))
}
```

Three more methods supply the blocks in the hyperparameters: the gradient,
the Hessian and the mixed block
$\partial^2\rho/\partial\beta\,\partial\theta$, which an outer search uses to
estimate the hyperparameters. Each of the three methods includes the `scale`
argument in its formals, because an S7 method must include the named
arguments of its generic and these three generics have one. The methods
return the derivatives on the parameter scale, and with `scale = "link"`
the generic carries them to the link scale through the links in
`link_params`.

```{r}
S7::method(penalty_grad_theta, BerhuPenalty) <- function(
    pen, beta, theta, scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...) {
  p <- .berhu(pen, beta, theta)
  list(lambda = sum(ifelse(p$big, (beta^2 + p$del^2) / (2 * p$del), p$a)),
       delta  = sum(ifelse(p$big,
                           p$lam * (p$del^2 - beta^2) / (2 * p$del^2), 0)))
}

S7::method(penalty_hess_theta, BerhuPenalty) <- function(
    pen, beta, theta, scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...) {
  p <- .berhu(pen, beta, theta)
  list(lambda_lambda = 0,
       delta_delta   = sum(ifelse(p$big, p$lam * beta^2 / p$del^3, 0)),
       lambda_delta  = sum(ifelse(p$big,
                                  (p$del^2 - beta^2) / (2 * p$del^2), 0)))
}

S7::method(penalty_cross, BerhuPenalty) <- function(
    pen, beta, theta, scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...) {
  p <- .berhu(pen, beta, theta)
  list(lambda = ifelse(p$big, beta / p$del, sign(beta)),
       delta  = ifelse(p$big, -p$lam * beta / p$del^2, 0))
}
```

The last two methods are `penalty_kinks()` and `is_proper()`.
`penalty_kinks()` returns the positions of the points at which some
derivative of the value is discontinuous, in the units of $D\beta$, and not
their number. The Berhu has
three such points. At the origin the first derivative jumps from $-\lambda$
to $\lambda$, and at $\pm\delta$ the first derivative is continuous while the
second jumps from $0$ to $\lambda/\delta$. SCAD has five, for the same two
reasons. The points at $\pm\delta$ move with the hyperparameter, so the
method reads `delta` from `theta`. `is_proper()` returns `FALSE`, because the
value defined above carries no normalizing constant and is therefore not the
negative log-density of a prior.

```{r}
S7::method(penalty_kinks, BerhuPenalty) <- function(pen, theta, ...) {
  c(0, -theta$delta, theta$delta)
}
S7::method(is_proper, BerhuPenalty) <- function(pen, ...) FALSE

pen <- berhu_penalty(5)
b <- c(-2.5, -0.4, 0, 0.7, 3.1)
th <- list(lambda = 1.3, delta = 1)

penalty_kinks(pen, th)
is_proper(pen)
penalty_value(pen, b, th)
penalty_gradient(pen, b, th)
diag(penalty_hessian(pen, b, th))
```

### The shapes of the hyperparameter blocks

Every hyperparameter block is a named list, not a matrix or a data frame.
`penalty_grad_theta()` returns one number per hyperparameter, keyed by
`pen@params`. `penalty_hess_theta()` returns one number per pair of
hyperparameters, keyed by the two names joined by an underscore: the diagonal
pairs come first, and then each remaining pair follows in the order of
`pen@params` (here `"lambda_lambda"`, `"delta_delta"` and `"lambda_delta"`).
`penalty_cross()` returns one vector of length `n_coef` per hyperparameter.
The generics read these names when they carry the blocks to the link scale.
A shipped penalty returns the same shapes:

```{r}
str(penalty_hess_theta(scad_penalty(n_coef = 3), c(-2, 0.3, 1.5),
                       list(lambda = 1, a = 3.7)))
```

## Validating it

`check_penalty()` compares each closed form with a numerical reference and
reports one row per comparison:

```{r}
print(check_penalty(pen, theta = th, verbose = FALSE))
```

The rows for the gradient in $\beta$ and in each hyperparameter
differentiate the value with `numDeriv`. The rows for the Hessian in
$\beta$, for every entry of the Hessian in the hyperparameters (including the
off-diagonal entry `lambda_delta`) and for the mixed block
differentiate the analytic first derivatives instead, with the Richardson
extrapolation of `numDeriv`, so that the value is never differenced twice.

### A numerical reference is invalid at a kink

If a coordinate of $\beta$ sits exactly on a kink, the check of the Hessian
fails on correct code:

```{r}
check_penalty(pen, beta = b, theta = th, verbose = FALSE)[1:2, ]
```

The vector `b` contains an exact zero. The gradient jumps from $-\lambda$ to
$\lambda$ there, so a central difference of the gradient across zero
measures the jump and not the formula. When `beta` is left `NULL`,
`check_penalty()` draws it from a fixed seed and shifts the draw until every
coordinate of $D\beta$ lies more than `0.05` from every point that
`penalty_kinks()` returns, and the first run passed because of this shift.
Moving the zero is enough:

```{r}
check_penalty(pen, beta = c(-2.5, -0.4, 0.05, 0.7, 3.1),
              theta = th, verbose = FALSE)[1:2, ]
```

For this reason `penalty_kinks()` returns the positions of the kinks and not
their number: `check_penalty()` needs the positions to keep its grid away
from them.

## Methods supplied by the base class

```{r}
c(is_quadratic   = is_quadratic(pen),
  beta_quadratic = beta_quadratic(pen, th),
  has_prox       = has_prox(pen))
penalty_draw(pen, th)
try(penalty_rank(pen))
```

The base class `penalty` has methods for the generics that a branch may
leave out. `is_quadratic()` and `beta_quadratic()` return `FALSE`,
`penalty_readable()` and `penalty_prox_spec()` return `NULL`, and
`penalty_draw()` returns `NA` for every coordinate of a penalty that is not
quadratic. `penalty_matrix()`, `penalty_rank()`, `penalty_null_basis()` and
`penalty_logpdet()` signal an error, because a rank, a null basis and a log
pseudo-determinant are properties of a quadratic form and the Berhu has no
matrix. `penalty_prox()` signals an error, and so do `penalty_dhessian()`,
`penalty_d2hessian()` and `penalty_dcross()`, the derivatives that a Laplace
approximation to a marginal likelihood needs, and the three generics for the
derivatives of the Hessian in $\beta$ (`penalty_dhessian_beta()`,
`penalty_d2hessian_beta()` and `penalty_dhessian_beta_theta()`). The
hyperparameters of the Berhu as written here therefore cannot be estimated
by a marginal criterion.

`has_prox()` returns `FALSE` because the Berhu has no method for
`penalty_prox()`. statmodels7 routes a block by whether `penalty_kinks()`
returns a point. A smooth penalty joins the Newton-type system of the other
coefficients, and a penalty with a kink is fitted by a proximal gradient
iteration, which calls `penalty_prox()`, or by a coordinate descent, which
reads `penalty_prox_spec()`. A penalty with a kink and without a method for
`penalty_prox()` can be evaluated and differentiated away from its kinks,
but it cannot be fitted by either scheme.

The proximal operator of the Berhu has a closed form, piecewise linear in
$v$, so a method for `penalty_prox()` can be registered in the same way as
the methods above. `penalty_prox_spec()` returns the same operator as a
piecewise-linear table, which the compiled coordinate descent reads. The
method of the base class returns `NULL`, and statmodels7 then fits the block
by the proximal gradient iteration.

## The normalizing constant is kept

A separable penalty built from a distributions7 family is the negative
log-density of that family, and the shipped ones keep the constant. The
lasso is a Laplace at zero in its rate parametrization, so its value carries
$-\log(\lambda/2)$ per coefficient:

```{r}
pen2 <- berhu_penalty(2)
small <- c(-0.3, 0.2)
c(berhu = penalty_value(pen2, small, th),
  lasso = penalty_value(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 2), small,
                        list(lambda = 1.3)),
  constant = -2 * log(1.3 / 2))
```

Without the constant the hyperparameters cannot be estimated: the objective
falls monotonically as $\lambda \to 0$, and the degrees of freedom of a $t$
prior cannot be estimated at all. The Berhu above has no constant, because
its value is not a normalized density, and for that reason its `is_proper()`
method returns `FALSE`. Its hyperparameters are set by the caller or chosen
by a criterion on prediction error, not by a marginal likelihood.

## Summary

* Minimum to define a penalty: a subclass of `penalty` and methods for
  `penalty_value()`, `penalty_gradient()`, `penalty_hessian()`,
  `penalty_grad_theta()`, `penalty_hess_theta()`, `penalty_cross()`,
  `penalty_kinks()` and `is_proper()`.
* The three hyperparameter blocks take a `scale` argument, because their
  generics declare one. Each returns a named list on the parameter scale,
  and the generic carries it to the link scale.
* `penalty_kinks()` returns positions, so that a numerical reference can be
  kept away from them.
* `check_penalty()` compares the gradients with `numDeriv` on the value and
  the second derivatives with `numDeriv` on the analytic gradients, including
  every entry of the hyperparameter Hessian. When it is given no $\beta$
  it draws one away from every declared kink.
* `is_quadratic()`, `beta_quadratic()`, `penalty_readable()`,
  `penalty_draw()`, `penalty_prox_spec()`, `penalty_matrix()`,
  `penalty_rank()`, `penalty_null_basis()`, `penalty_logpdet()`,
  `penalty_prox()`, `penalty_dhessian()` and its siblings have methods on the
  base class. The first five return `FALSE`, `NULL` or `NA`; the others
  signal an error for a penalty that is not quadratic or has no such method.
* `has_prox()` is `FALSE` until a method for `penalty_prox()` is registered,
  and a fit of a penalty with a kink needs that method.
